name: forge-survey
_note: OMEGA FORGE Wave 1+ builder composition (D-417 §5 lane 3) — the survey boot: vivim.law (phase 0, gate + journal + the consent ceremony), vivim.vault (the proposal ledger that HOLDS the capture receipt and its CAS blobs), forge.mine.capture (the ONE filesystem seam, booted here so a receipt and its blobs EXIST in this ledger — forge.mine.capture@1 routed normally, EXTERNAL_MUTATION so the host gates it through law.check@1 before the handler ever reads a byte; the caller performs the two-principal consent ceremony), and forge.survey (READ — forge.survey.run@1 / forge.survey.render@1, granted exactly the two read-only vault ports they use: get for the receipt row, bounded getmany batches for the blobs). Survey reads the snapshot AS STORED and never re-walks the mine tree: there is no node:fs import in its compartment and no filesystem capability in its grant, which is what keeps D-409's class split honest. The capture entry's grant set is IDENTICAL to the one in forge-mine.json and forge-mine-capture.json (append + get + getmany + law.check): compositions.ts check 4 fingerprints every plugin's grant across compositions and flags any variance with no DRIFT_ALLOWLIST entry, and the identity is also functionally required — without the getmany grant the capture's own blob read-back is capability-refused there. The vivim.law entry is copied VERBATIM from those compositions including law.consent.grant@1: the whole capture ceremony runs through it, and vivim.law IS DRIFT_ALLOWLISTed, so a divergent law grant would fail SILENTLY — every capture gate-refused and the suite could never produce its own evidence. This is a builder composition — no product composition may route forge.* ops (FORGE_IN_PRODUCT).
